findings.title: TLS1.0 negotiated
findings.description: This session negotiated TLS1.0. TLS 1.0 is deprecated (NIST SP 800-52r2 disallows below 1.2; RFC 8996). NIST SP 800-52r2 and RFC 8996 require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 for email transport.
findings.reference: NIST SP 800-52r2 §3.1; RFC 8996; OWASP TLS Cheat Sheet §'understand TLS 1.2'

findings.title: RC4 negotiated
findings.description: TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA uses the RC4 stream cipher. RC4 biases allow practical plaintext recovery (Bar-Mitzvah/BEAST variants) and it is prohibited in RFC 7465 for TLS.
findings.reference: RFC 7465; NIST SP 800-52r2 App A

findings.title: TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA uses legacy bulk encryption
findings.description: The negotiated cipher TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA does not use an authenticated AEAD mode (AES-GCM/CCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305). CBC-mode ciphers are subject to padding-oracle attacks (e.g. Lucky13) and lack integrity protection the same way. Prefer AEAD ciphers (NIST SP 800-52r2 preference).
findings.reference: NIST SP 800-52r2 §3.3.1; OWASP TLS Cheat Sheet

findings.title: TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA uses static key exchange
findings.description: The negotiated cipher TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA does not use ephemeral (EC)DHE key exchange. If the server private key is compromised, all past sessions can be decrypted (no forward secrecy). Prefer ECDHE suites.
findings.reference: NIST SP 800-52r2 §3.3.1; OWASP TLS Cheat Sheet §'use forward secrecy'

findings.title: ClientHello advertises no ECDHE/DHE cipher suites
findings.description: The client's offered cipher list contains no ephemeral-DH suites, so a PFS-capable server will fall back to a static key exchange if this client is relicensed maintenance.
findings.reference: OWASP TLS Cheat Sheet §'use forward secrecy'

findings.title: STARTTLS advertised but no handshake followed
findings.description: The SMTP server advertised STARTTLS capability (or the client requested it) but the session proceeded without a TLS handshake. An active attacker may have suppressed/forged the STARTTLS response to force plaintext (STRIPTLS / STARTTLS downgrade). Clients MUST refuse to continue when STARTTLS is not honored.
findings.reference: RFC 3207 §4.1.2; OWASP SMTP Transport Security through STARTTLS

findings.title: Email credentials/messages sent in cleartext
findings.description: SMTP session carried no TLS. If STARTTLS was expected this is a protocol-stripping / MITM indicator; credentials and message bodies were transmitted in cleartext and are recoverable from the capture.
findings.reference: RFC 3207 §4 (SMTP); NIST SP 800-52r2 §3.3
